meta.title: Two-Phase Commit: Atomic Commit Across Two Databases

segments.label: Phase 1: Prepare — coordinator asks everyone to promise
Phase 2: Commit — only sent after both vote yes

cards.title: The Blocking Problem
items: If the coordinator crashes after both vote yes but before sending COMMIT, both participants are stuck
They hold locks and can't unilaterally decide to commit or abort — they must wait for the coordinator to recover
This is 2PC's core weakness: it trades progress for atomicity

cards.title: Why Voting Yes Is a Real Promise
items: A participant can still abort during Prepare, e.g. a constraint violation or lock timeout
Once it votes yes, it must be able to commit even after its own crash and restart — so the vote and pre-commit state are written to disk before replying
Only after every participant votes yes does the coordinator move to Phase 2

cards.title: Alternatives at Scale
items: Three-phase commit adds a round trip to reduce the blocking window, but is rarely used in practice
Distributed databases increasingly avoid cross-node 2PC by using a single consensus log (Raft/Paxos) instead
Application-level sagas trade atomicity for availability: each step commits locally and failures trigger compensating actions
